jobs.prompt: A clean, professional infographic diagram on a very light warm orange tinted background, subtle peachy tone. Flat design, modern tech style. Title at top center in bold dark sans-serif text: 'Git with Claude Code — Just Tell It What You Want'. The diagram shows 4 steps arranged in a horizontal row from left to right. Each step is a rounded card with a large circled number at the top. STEP 1 card has a small gray tag 'one-time' at the top corner. Inside: bold heading 'Connect to GitHub'. Below in a chat bubble style with orange border: the user prompt text 'Connect this folder to my repo via SSH'. Below that, in a smaller monospace code block with gray background: 'git remote add origin git@...'. STEP 2 card also has a small gray tag 'one-time'. Inside: bold heading 'First Push'. Chat bubble: 'Do the initial commit and push everything'. Code block: 'git add . → git commit → git push -u origin main'. STEP 3 card is visually LARGER and HIGHLIGHTED with an orange border and very light orange fill, with a prominent tag 'daily workflow' in orange. Inside: bold heading 'Save Your Work'. Chat bubble: 'Commit and push'. Code block: 'git add . → git commit -m msg → git push'. A circular arrow icon suggests repetition. STEP 4 card has a small tag 'when needed'. Inside: bold heading 'Go Back'. Chat bubble: 'Revert to the previous commit'. Code block: 'git revert HEAD'. A small curved arrow pointing backward. Between all steps, thin arrow lines connect them left to right. Step 4 has a curved dashed arrow going back toward step 3 to show the recovery loop. At the bottom center, a small note: 'You type plain English — Claude Code runs the git commands'. Top-left corner and top-right corner completely empty. Flat vector infographic, no photorealism, no 3D, clean layout, generous whitespace.

A clean, minimal infographic diagram with very subtle light warm orange wash background. Modern flat design. Title at top center in clean dark sans-serif font: 'Your Git Cheat Sheet for Claude Code'. Subtitle in smaller gray text: 'You type simple commands. Claude Code handles the rest.' The diagram is arranged as 4 vertical rows, each row representing one step. Each row has three columns: LEFT column shows a large step number in an orange circle and a label. MIDDLE column shows what the user types in a rounded chat bubble with orange accent. RIGHT column shows what happens behind the scenes in a gray monospace code block. ROW 1: Step number '1' with gray label 'Setup (once)'. Chat bubble: 'Connect this folder to my GitHub repo via SSH'. Code block: 'git remote add origin git@github.com:user/repo.git'. ROW 2: Step number '2' with gray label 'Setup (once)'. Chat bubble: 'Initial commit and push everything'. Code block: 'git add . → git commit -m initial → git push -u origin main'. ROW 3: Step number '3' with label 'Daily workflow' in BOLD ORANGE TEXT, this entire row has a very subtle orange highlight background to emphasize it is the main action. Chat bubble: 'Commit and push'. Code block: 'git add . → git commit -m changes → git push'. A small repeat icon or infinity symbol next to it. ROW 4: Step number '4' with gray label 'Recovery'. Chat bubble: 'Revert to previous commit'. Code block: 'git revert HEAD'. A small undo arrow icon. A thin horizontal line separates the setup rows (1-2) from the workflow rows (3-4). On the left side, a bracket groups rows 1-2 with label 'one-time setup' and rows 3-4 with label 'ongoing'. Top-left corner and top-right corner completely empty with consistent background. Pure flat vector infographic, clean geometric shapes, generous whitespace, very readable.
